accepted: شْحَال دْيَال الْوَقْت غَادِي يَاخُد الطّْلَب؟
شحال ديال الوقت غادي ياخد الطلب؟
sh7aal dyaal lweqt ghaadi yaakhod TTalab?

too_formal.feedback: Correct Modern Standard Arabic, but not how it is said at a counter in Casablanca or Rabat.

exercises.tip: "شحال ديال الوقت" is how much time.

phrases.arabic: الْمَرَّة الْجَّايَة عَنْدْنَا، إِن شَاء اللَّه
phrases.english: Next time it's at our place, God willing.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا بيك آ أمين، الدار دارك.
dialogue.transliteration: mar7ba beek a Ameen, ddaar daarek.
dialogue.english: Welcome, Amine, make yourself at home.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: الله يعز قدرك. يالاه، الماكلة واجدة.
dialogue.transliteration: llaah y3ezz qedrek. yallaah, lmaakla waajda.
dialogue.english: You're too kind. Come on, the food is ready.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: آ آدم، كول بيدك اليمنى آ وليدي.
dialogue.transliteration: a Aadam, kool b yeddek lymna a wleedi.
dialogue.english: Adam, eat with your right hand, son.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.english: Really, don't be shy, have more!

pair.english: Shall we have tea after the meal?

lessons.culture: A Moroccan host offers more food again and again, and a guest usually refuses a couple of times before giving in. After the meal guests say "الله يخلف" or "الله يجازيك بخير" and the host answers "بالصحة والراحة"; the meal often ends with mint tea (أتاي) poured by the host.

exercises.prompt: Your host says: "زيد كول شوية." Say thank God, you're full.

too_formal.feedback: Correct Modern Standard Arabic, but not how it is said at a counter in Casablanca or Rabat.

exercises.tip: "شبعت" is I'm full; a woman says the same.

exercises.prompt: You thank your host: "الله يجازيك بخير." What does the host answer?

too_formal.feedback: Correct and pious, but bookish; the everyday Moroccan host's answer is "بالصحة والراحة".

exercises.tip: "بالصحة" wishes the guest good health from the food.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شكرا على _____." Meaning: Thank you for the invitation.

too_formal.feedback: "الدعوة" is understood but in Darija an invitation to eat is "العرضة".

exercises.tip: "عرض" is to invite someone to a meal.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شحال _____ هاد الماكلة!" Meaning: How delicious this food is!

too_formal.feedback: "لذيذ" is understood but formal; Moroccans say "بنين".

exercises.tip: "الماكلة" is feminine, so it is "بنينة".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Please pass me the water."

too_formal.feedback: Correct Modern Standard Arabic, but not how it is said at a counter in Casablanca or Rabat.

exercises.tip: Water is "الما" in Darija.

exercises.prompt: Translate (to a man): "Please come in and sit down."

too_formal.feedback: Correct Modern Standard Arabic, but not how it is said at a counter in Casablanca or Rabat.

exercises.tip: To a woman: "تفضلي، دخلي وجلسي".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Shall we have tea after the meal?"

too_formal.feedback: MSA; Moroccan tea is "أتاي" and food is "الماكلة".

exercises.tip: The "و" at the end of "نشربو" means we.

exercises.prompt: Which one does a guest say before starting to eat?
exercises.tip: Say it before eating; if you forget, say "بسم الله أوله وآخره".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Next time it's at our place"?
exercises.answer: الْمَرَّة الْجَّايَة عَنْدْنَا، إِن شَاء اللَّه
options: الْمَرَّة الْجَّايَة عَنْدْنَا، إِن شَاء اللَّه
accepted: الْمَرَّة الْجَّايَة عَنْدْنَا، إِن شَاء اللَّه
المرة الجاية عندنا إن شاء الله

too_formal.feedback: Correct Modern Standard Arabic, but not how it is said at a counter in Casablanca or Rabat.

exercises.tip: "الجاية" means the coming one, the next.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: Eat with your right hand.

too_formal.feedback: Nearly the same; Darija says "كول" with a long vowel.

exercises.tip: "يدّك" is your hand.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: I am honoured by your invitation.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA wording; Darija uses "العرضة ديالك".

exercises.tip: "ديالك" means your.

challenge.title: At the Restaurant
challenge.instructions: Have a full conversation ordering a drink and a meal at a Casablanca restaurant, then ask for and settle the bill.
required_elements: Ask what's on the menu or what's recommended
Order at least one drink and one dish, including one preference (e.g. no onion, extra bread, sweet or no sugar)
Ask for the bill and how much it costs
Say something to close the meal, like a compliment to the food or a thank you

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.english: What do you recommend I get?

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.arabic: الطاجين د الدجاج مزيان بزاف هنا
dialogue.transliteration: ttajin d ddjaaj mzyaan bzaf hna
dialogue.english: The chicken tagine is really good here.

dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.transliteration: wakha, ghaadi nakhud ttajin w atay b nna3na3
dialogue.english: Okay, I'll have the tagine and mint tea.

dialogue.speaker: Waiter

dialogue.speaker: Waiter
dialogue.english: Okay, coming now.

dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.speaker: You
